comparison: Perfect agreement on ECG findings (C28-C33). Both evaluations support the age-related effects on cardiac aperiodic activity across four datasets with ~2300 participants. OpenEval notes the steepening in CamCAN dataset requires investigation; peer reviewers accepted findings without critique.

Perfect agreement on cognitive modulation findings (C67-C69). Both strongly support the working memory task results. OpenEval notes this is preliminary/outlook analysis; peer reviewer enthusiastically endorsed it, suggesting it 'practically warrants a separate paper.'

Perfect agreement on simulation results (C42). Both support the simulation demonstrating cardiac influence on combined spectra. OpenEval acknowledges simulation limitations; peer reviewers found analyses 'compelling, convincing, thorough, and measured.'

Perfect agreement on methodological considerations (C83-C87). Both support the discussion of ICA limitations and recommendations. OpenEval notes appropriate citations; peer reviewers found the discussion 'very clear' regarding multiple sources of aperiodic activity.

Strong agreement on MEG findings (C43-C52). Both support the multiverse analysis showing cardiac influence. OpenEval notes unexpected steepening contradicts EEG literature; peer reviewers commended the multiverse approach and replication efforts. Peer review includes C53 not in OpenEval grouping.

Strong agreement on literature analysis (C22-C25). Both support the systematic analysis of 279 articles. OpenEval emphasizes explicit methodology; peer reviewer praised it as 'very clever, and expanded upon from any other prior version.' OpenEval includes C26 which peer review addresses separately.

Agreement on mechanistic discussion (C66, C70-C78). Both acknowledge this as appropriate speculative discussion. OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting these are hypotheses requiring testing; peer reviewers found the in-depth discussion valuable and noted authors address vagueness about higher frequency ECG contributions.

Strong agreement on pharmacological implications (C91-C97, C99). Both support the discussion of potential confounding in drug studies. OpenEval notes appropriate caution; peer reviewer specifically praised the 'excellent commentary regarding physiological effects' of propofol and ketamine.

Agreement on TRF/decoding findings (C36-C41) but different scope. Both support evidence of residual cardiac activity after ICA. OpenEval focuses on TRF analysis claims; peer review additionally includes broader conclusions (C82, C98, C105) about ICA limitations and cardiac influence.

Agreement on regression analyses (C54-C57) but different scope. Both support unique variance contributions. OpenEval focuses on statistical approach; peer review additionally includes core conclusions (C88, C107, C108) about cardiac vs. neural contributions to age effects.

Agreement on control analyses (C63-C65) with different emphasis. Both support robustness checks including replication. OpenEval emphasizes convergence across approaches; peer reviewers commended efforts but noted head movement as imperfect proxy for muscle activity.

Partial overlap on literature analysis. Both support findings about field practices. OpenEval groups C22-C26 together; peer review separately addresses C26-C27 about methodological variability, praising the 'clever' literature analysis.

Overlap on primary conclusions (C88, C107). OpenEval groups these with C5 as central finding integrating all results; peer review groups them with regression analyses (C54-C57, C108), emphasizing cardiac contribution exceeds neural influence on age-related aperiodic activity.

Overlap on ICA limitations (C82, C105). OpenEval groups these with C6 about residual ECG after ICA; peer review groups them with TRF findings (C36-C41, C98), emphasizing cardiac activity remains even after sensitive ICA thresholds.

Minimal overlap on frequency-dependent effects (C108). OpenEval groups C7-C8, C108 about unique variance at different frequencies; peer review includes C108 with broader conclusions about cardiac vs. neural contributions to age effects.

OpenEval evaluated established literature foundation (C1-C21) as appropriately cited background knowledge. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; reviewers focused on novel empirical findings rather than background claims.

OpenEval rated C35 (similarity across modalities) as UNCERTAIN due to inconsistent steepening/flattening patterns across ECG datasets and MEG. No corresponding peer review evaluation found addressing this specific cross-modality comparison claim.

OpenEval evaluated limitations discussion (C100-C103) as appropriately cited acknowledgments of factors beyond study scope. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; reviewers did not specifically comment on these limitation statements.

OpenEval evaluated conclusions and recommendations (C104, C106, C109) as supported and actionable. No corresponding peer review evaluation found specifically addressing these recommendation claims, though reviewers generally endorsed the study's conclusions.

OpenEval evaluated methodological reporting (C4, C110-C112) as appropriately documented standard procedures. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; reviewers did not comment on basic methodological documentation claims.
